note: Fixed before any v2 evaluation data was generated or viewed. Changes after the pre-registration commit are allowed only as a dated amendment in DECISIONS.md; old values stay in git history. The constants below were chosen from the statistic's definition and general practice (Bonferroni 0.05, a 20-peer floor for a quantile-based gap, a 40-line volume floor shared with v1), not from any ClaimSignal label or score.

v2.status: experimental; not wired into the API, dossier or agent; v1 stays the product default unless the owner decides otherwise
algorithm: peers = same-specialty providers with at least MIN_VISIT_LINES visit lines, subject excluded
abstain if the subject has fewer than MIN_VISIT_LINES visit lines, if fewer than MIN_PEERS peers exist, or if the peer median high-level share is at or above PEER_MEDIAN_ABSTAIN_AT
p0 = peer median high-level share clamped to [P0_FLOOR, P0_CAP]
p_value = one-sided exact binomial upper tail P(X >= x), X ~ Binomial(n = subject visit lines, p0), x = subject highest-level lines
gap = subject high-level share minus the peers' 75th percentile (statistics.quantiles, n=4, inclusive)
flag iff p_value <= alpha_adjusted AND gap >= MIN_GAP_ABOVE_P75; otherwise no_flag

hypotheses.H1: On fresh independent data, v2 finds at least 0.80 of scorable TRUE providers in the primary specialties.
hypotheses.H2: v2 recall exceeds v1 recall on the same fixture by at least 0.20 (absolute).
hypotheses.H3: v2 raises at most 5% of scorable ORDINARY and DECOY providers combined in the primary specialties.
hypotheses.H4: v2 raises no more ORDINARY or DECOY providers than v1 on the same fixture.

data_requirements.author: an isolated model task that sees only the brief; it must not receive earlier results, earlier independent data, the detector, its constants or expected outcomes
must_include: volumes from about 10 to about 800 visit lines
providers below and above the volume floor in every primary specialty
a declared high-contamination stratum analysed separately
data_requirements.sealing: labels.jsonl, providers.jsonl, rules.json and AUTHOR_NOTE.md are hashed on receipt and the hashes committed before any detector is run; labels are read only by the scorer
data_requirements.validation: evals/intensity_v2.py validates schema and the prevalence, volume and stratum requirements before scoring and reports every problem; nothing is repaired

scoring.scorable: a provider with at least 40 visit lines (the volume floor both versions share)
scoring.primary_scope: providers in the primary specialties (S1 to S3)
scoring.v1_abstain: provider_intensity returns no metrics and a 'Not scored' limit
scoring.v2_abstain: provider_intensity_v2 decision is abstain; an abstention on a scorable TRUE provider counts as a miss

primary.recall: flagged scorable TRUE providers / scorable TRUE providers, primary specialties pooled
primary.false_positive_rate: flagged scorable (ORDINARY + DECOY) providers / scorable (ORDINARY + DECOY) providers, primary specialties pooled
primary.false_alarm_count: flagged scorable (ORDINARY + DECOY) providers, primary specialties pooled

secondary: recall by specialty, by severity (mild, strong) and by volume band
false-positive rate for ORDINARY only, DECOY only, hard DECOY only
recall over all TRUE providers including those below the volume floor
every abstention with its reason, by label
the contamination stratum (S4): recall, false positives and abstentions for both versions, reported separately and never pooled into the gate
v1 and v2 outcomes on every provider in a per-provider table

failure_handling: If any gate fails, v2 stays experimental, v1 stays the product default, and the miss is recorded in KNOWN_FAILURES.md with the numbers. No constant is changed and the same fixture is not re-scored with different constants.
A different v2 design needs a new pre-registration and a fresh fixture from a new author.

If the delivery fails schema validation, the author may be asked once to correct schema errors only (not data content); every problem and the re-delivery are recorded. Content requirements (prevalence, volume bands, strata) that fail validation are recorded as a limit of the test, not repaired by the main agent.
Both versions are scored on exactly the same fixture and both results are reported whatever the outcome.
The main agent does not edit providers.jsonl, labels.jsonl or rules.json.
known_limits_stated_in_advance: The brief was written by the main agent, which knows the v2 design; the brief contains no detector constants, but the test is not blind on the brief side.
The fixture author is a model, not a human, and labels are not human-reviewed.
Aggregated visit counts replace claim-level data; v1 and v2 both run through the real repository path on claims generated deterministically from those counts.
A different-family author (preferred) may be unavailable in this environment; the author model actually used is recorded.
A single fixture of this size gives wide intervals; a pass is evidence on synthetic data only, not real-world performance.
